prompt: Roadmap III, Prompt 217, eclipsing binaries: a detached model with identifiability stated (tranche T3 by D-R10-207-01)
committed: before js/stellar/binaries.js, the inference model, the validator, the oracle script, its pinned results, the ensembles, the panel or any lesson of Prompt 217 existed. The systems, seeds, cadences and noise below are written out so that the oracle and the harness build identical inputs; nothing was tuned against the kernel, which did not exist.
rule: A crossed bound is a failed check, recorded in failed-legs.json and left failing; only Carl resets one. A leg that cannot be measured is NOT RUN and says why.

scope.built: a detached eclipsing binary: two spheres on a Keplerian orbit (circular or eccentric), radii as fractions of the semi-major axis a (rsum = (R1+R2)/a, k = R2/R1), central surface brightness ratio J = S2/S1 in one band, quadratic limb darkening for each star (coefficients are settings from a cited table, never fitted by default), optional fixed third light, the eclipse geometry (contacts, depth, durations), the eclipse timing relations (e cos w from the secondary's phase, e sin w from the duration ratio), and a fit through the inference core (js/inference/fit.js, rank and profile) whose result says, parameter by parameter, whether the data constrain it.
scope.notBuilt: reflection, ellipsoidal variation, Doppler beaming, gravity darkening, spots, pulsation, light-travel time across the orbit, apsidal motion, third bodies, a distance or a mass (218). The model refuses nothing about a system that has these effects; it says so in its notClaimed and the residual test shows them.

convention: Star 1 is the star eclipsed at the primary eclipse (star 2 in front of it, at the time tc of that conjunction); J <= 1 so that star 1 has the higher central surface brightness and the primary eclipse is the deeper one. w is the argument of periastron of the orbit of star 2 relative to star 1, as in Winn (2010): the primary eclipse is at true anomaly pi/2 - w, and e cos w > 0 puts the secondary eclipse after phase 0.5. The argument of periastron of the primary star's own orbit, used for radial velocities, is w + 180 degrees.

S3.what: star 2 the larger and cooler (k > 1), total at primary

circular.what: C1 and the control of D1, D2

grazing.what: D1: the minimum sky separation is 0.93 of r1 + r2, so the eclipse is a thin lens

spotted.what: D2: the circular system plus an out-of-eclipse modulation the model does not have

modulation.form: multiply by 1 + amplitude * sin(2 pi t / period + phase)

checks.what: central eclipses (inc 90, circular): the primary and secondary depth of uniform stars against k^2/(1+J k^2) and J/(1+J k^2) (star 2 smaller: the primary is a transit of star 1, the secondary hides star 2 totally; star 2 larger: the reverse), and for limb-darkened stars the blocked fraction by Simpson quadrature of the stated law

first and fourth contact: the flux is exactly 1 one microday outside the contact time and below 1 one microday inside it, the contact time found by an independent bisection of the sky separation against r1 + r2 (own Kepler solver in the validator), for the circular and the eccentric systems; the circular total duration against sin(pi T / P) = sqrt((r1+r2)^2 - cos^2 i) / sin i

the phase of the secondary conjunction against the exact closed form at inc 90 (Sterne 1939): 0.5 + (1/pi) [arctan(x / sqrt(1-e^2)) + x sqrt(1-e^2) / (1 - e^2 sin^2 w)], x = e cos w, both signs of x and all four quadrants of w
the curve is the same when the stars are exchanged: k -> 1/k, J -> 1/J, limb darkening swapped, w -> w + 180, tc -> the secondary conjunction (S1, S2, S3)
the flux is exactly 1 outside every eclipse (S1, S2, S3, 4000 phases), never above 1, and third light l3 gives (1 - l3) F + l3 to rounding

the derived quantities from their definitions: r1 = rsum/(1+k), r2 = k r1, e = hypot(e cos w, e sin w), w = atan2, the light ratio L2/L1 = J k^2 (1 - uB1/3 - uB2/6)/(1 - uA1/3 - uA2/6), the impact parameter cos i / r1
the first-order inversion e cos w = (pi/2)(phase_secondary - 0.5) against the truth, over e up to 0.3 and every w
the ratio of the secondary's duration to the primary's, from exact contacts at inc 89, against (1 + e sin w)/(1 - e sin w) (Winn 2010, eq. 16), for e <= 0.1

the whole light curve of S1, S2 and S3 on 2000 phases against batman 2.5.1 (Kreidberg 2015, PASP 127, 1161): the eclipse of each star computed by batman as a transit of that star by the other (the second in the swapped frame), weighted by the light ratio; independent of this repository's code

S1 and S3 against a brute-force 2-D polar quadrature of the two eclipsed discs (1200 radial by 2400 angular cells), a second independent implementation that needs no analytic formula, for the case k > 1 included
the secondary conjunction time of S2 and S3 against batman's t_secondary, and the primary and secondary minimum depths against batman's
the 1-sigma interval of the fit (the covariance, scaled by sqrt(chi2/dof) when above 1) holds the truth at the stated rate for rsum, k, inc, J, tc and P on 120 seeds of the circular ensemble
the same on 120 seeds of the eccentric ensemble, with e cos w and e sin w free
the Delta chi^2 = 1 profile interval for rsum, k and inc holds the truth at the stated rate on the first 40 seeds of the circular ensemble
the median fitted value of each parameter over the circular ensemble is within 3 median sigma / sqrt(n) of the truth (no bias beyond the statistical)

the grazing system is flagged: at least 90% of 40 seeds return identifiability 'not constrained' for the radius ratio k; the control (the first 60 seeds of the circular ensemble) is flagged at most 5%. The rule is fixed here: k is not constrained when the rank analysis of js/inference/fit.js lists it, or its uncertainty exceeds 25% of its value, or it sits on a bound

the misspecified (spotted) system fails the stated residual test on at least 95% of 20 seeds, and the correct model on at most 5% of the first 60 circular seeds. The test is fixed here: reduced chi^2 above 1.5, or the red-noise factor beta above 1.5
noise only (20 seeds) is refused with a message that names the missing eclipse, never fitted
the eccentric system fitted with e fixed at 0 fails the same residual test on at least 95% of 20 seeds
in the eccentric ensemble the median uncertainty of e sin w is at least 5 times that of e cos w

V505 Persei (TIC 348517784), TESS Sector 18, SPOC 2-minute SAP_FLUX with QUALITY = 0, against Southworth (2021), The Observatory 141, 'Rediscussion of eclipsing binaries. Paper VI' (arXiv:2106.04323), Table II. The contract: each eclipse (primary at phase 0, secondary at 0.5, by the paper's ephemeris) windowed to +-1.0 T14 about its midpoint (T14 from the paper's solution), each window divided by a straight line fitted to its points beyond 0.55 T14 from the midpoint; a constant uncertainty from those out-of-eclipse residuals; circular orbit, limb darkening fixed at the paper's linear 0.261 and quadratic 0.23 for both stars, third light 0; fitted tc, P, rsum, k, inc, J. The paper's values were not used to tune anything: they are read here only to be compared.

limits.note: JKTEBOP (version 41) includes a reflection effect and fits nine out-of-eclipse straight lines; this model has neither, and its eclipse windows are normalised before the fit, so the 2-sigma bound is a real test, not a formality. The data file is not in the repository; the leg is NOT RUN without it.

checks.what: one fit of the circular ensemble's first seed (1,380 rows) with its profiles skipped runs in at most 10 s of CPU on the machine, recorded and not a physics bound
